pos.personaBrief: Fluminense had about 70% possession in the Libertadores final and stayed committed to building from the back even when 1-0 up (TSG), and Diniz is associated with having the ball; the ball is the team's control and defence.

pro.personaBrief: Short-touch build-up from the keeper, André dropping between the centre-backs, and a pressed build-up with 'coragem para jogar' (TSG, TFA, Trivela); rotation and technical players are involved from the first phase.

est.personaBrief: Diniz calls his game 'anti-positional/aposicional': players migrate, 7-8 gather on one side, and fluidity replaces fixed positions (Sky, Netflu, NYT, Trivela).

lar.personaBrief: Full-backs come inside, wingers combine on the same flank in tabelas (Keno-Arias), overloads on one side then a switch (TSG); play is built around close central-and-half-space combinations more than touchline crossing.

blo.personaBrief: PPDA 7.33, forwards start the press from the goal kick, high line, counter-pressing after losses, and Diniz said 'a tendência é marcar alto' (Coaches' Voice, TFA, TSG, Netflu Feb 2023).

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence on this axis, so this comes from general knowledge: Diniz's team defends with encaixes and zone-oriented handoffs inside a compact block, without dedicated man-marking of stars, consistent with the verified fluid, space-oriented pressing.

pla.personaBrief: Diniz kept his style against Manchester City ('Nós não erramos por causa do estilo') and kept 'coragem para jogar' as a mantra; he did a different plan against Olimpia but within his characteristics, and imposed his model on arrival.

res.personaBrief: Diniz sticks to the style even in the Club World Cup final against City and does not usually take off a defender to protect leads (Trivela), while still winning the Libertadores; style is central to his idea.

sis.personaBrief: The collective idea of rotation and proximity is the core, but it is built around technical players like Ganso, Keno and Arias with positional freedom (TFA, Blizzard); everyone presses and works though.

jog.personaBrief: Technical players such as Ganso as the maestro, André and Felipe Melo as passers, and Diniz's psychology and futsal-influenced technical play; intensity is also required (aggressive press, trainings like war).

bas.personaBrief: The title side leaned on veterans (Fábio, Felipe Melo, Marcelo, Ganso) with the same eleven in the final, yet Diniz trusted John Kennedy and Lelê and the academy was not central to the squad.

lid.personaBrief: Diniz is a psychology graduate who manages and motivates in a particular way, protects John Kennedy and gives rest days (Sky, Colunadofla, Trivela), though trainings are described as war; more harmony than iron fist.
